title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from satellite innovations to budget increases aimed at resilience. Meanwhile, the commercial space landscape continues to evolve, with notable funding rounds and strategic partnerships making headlines.

themes.title: Satellite Innovations Abound
themes.body: Muon Space's unveiling of a Starship-class satellite platform signals a push towards orbital data centers, while Murata's exploration of Xona's timing service hints at telecom's growing reliance on space tech. These developments could redefine how data is managed in orbit.

themes.title: Defense Budgets on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion boost for space resilience reflects a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space in defense. This could pave the way for enhanced capabilities, especially as threats evolve.

themes.title: Commercial Space Gains Traction
themes.body: With Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C, the commercial sector is clearly gaining momentum. The increasing interest from venture capitalists suggests a belief that space is not just a frontier, but a lucrative market.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions in Orbit
themes.body: Russian co-orbital activity near commercial GEO slots raises concerns about the security of space assets, while GPS jamming in the Eastern Mediterranean returns to pre-2024 levels. These developments underscore the need for robust space situational awareness.
